## The 3 best new ideas worth adopting

1. **The partition date anchor.** The partition is dated 15 Mar 2017 and is supposed to implement a plan that, according to Exh. C on the face of the Balane title, was surveyed 8 Sep 2020 and approved 6 Apr 2021. Cesar died 21 Jun 2017. His Deed of Confirmation was registered 23 Nov 2021, after his death. This is pure documents, needs no witness, uses no adjective, and goes straight at Answer ¶46 and at "no approved plan in 2016". Put it in the case-in-chief (Exh. B and Exh. C are already marked). Hold only the notarial register.
2. **"Doors" the defense has already opened.** The deed recites that Art. 1623 notice to co-owners "had been complied with". The receipts are headed "Heirs of Mary W. Keesey Estate". Erwin says the purchase began "first with Ben Llamanzares". Each is a defense claim of consent or notice that Patricia can answer on rebuttal under Rule 30 §5(f). This is the best solution yet to the problem of a rebuttal-only witness. Have counsel put each point to the defense witnesses on cross, and order every transcript.
3. **The demurrer-proof element matrix, plus the peso figure from cross.** Keep the table format, corrected per C1. Add the plan's damages fix: Art. 2234 requires a temperate or compensatory award before exemplary damages, and no witness has yet given a rental value. Ask Princess and Erwin on cross how many rooms are rented and for how much (Answer ¶27). Cheap, and it fills a real gap.

Runner-up: fix the checkable anchors now (Llamanzares's date of death, Violeta, the "brown columnar book", the receipt-book imprint) to defend against any late witness. Present them only as dates.
